items.title: Regularization delays leave hundreds of migrants in limbo
items.body: Out of 549,596 applications for Spain's extraordinary regularization process, only 91,905 have received approval to work provisionally, leaving over 50,000 people waiting beyond the promised 15-day timeline. Many migrants report waiting over 40 days without response, causing anxiety and uncertainty.

items.title: Housing prices do not fall despite market slowdown
items.body: Home prices rose 12.5% in 2025, pushing the effort rate to 8 years of income, a high since 2011. While sales have slowed, experts predict a 'cooling' but no price drop due to inflation and rising interest rates.

items.title: Autónomos can now work and collect full pension
items.body: A new law allows self-employed workers (autónomos) to return to work after retirement without losing their pension, provided they haven't been registered as autónomos for three years prior. The one-year waiting period has also been removed, making flexible retirement more accessible.

items.title: Bird flu causes egg price surge in Spain
items.body: Spain has culled 2.7 million laying hens (5.6% of the flock) due to avian flu since autumn, leading to a drop of 32.5 million dozen eggs in production. The supply shortage is contributing to rising egg prices at supermarkets.

items.title: Oil price swings amid Iran war and hopes for ceasefire
items.body: The ongoing conflict in Iran and threats to the Strait of Hormuz have sent oil prices on a volatile rollercoaster. Each shift in diplomatic messaging from Trump triggers price spikes or drops, impacting global costs of living.

items.title: PSOE official accused in conspiracy plot against corruption investigators
items.body: Former PSOE organization secretary Santos Cerdán is under investigation for allegedly orchestrating a conspiracy to find dirt on the Civil Guard and prosecutors investigating socialist corruption. The plot involved a party member and an entrepreneur and was reportedly financed by the PSOE.
